To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) morphic sequences are transductive, (b) non-erasing morphic images are alpha-substitutive for some alpha, (c) non-erasic transductions preserve alpha-substitutiveness, and (d) the intersection of two alpha-substitutive sequences is ultimately periodic.
the class of morphic sequences is closed under transduction (by a non-erasing morphism), and that non-erasure preserves alpha-substitutiveness.

(i) non-erasing finite state transductions preserve alpha-substitutability; (ii) for multiplicatively independent alpha and beta, no non-erasing image of an alpha-substitutitive sequence can be beta-substitutive; and (iii) for multiplicatively dependent alpha and beta, there are non-erasing images of alpha-substitutive sequences that are beta-substitutive.
In summary, our research is concerned with
eigenvalue properties of substitutions, and with transductions of morphic and automatic sequences.
the interplay between the algebraic structure and the combinatorial structure of infinite words.
the interplay between the eigenvalue spectrum of morphic sequences and their transduction spectrum.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the transduction of automatic, morphic, or alpha-substitutive sequences is a well-behaved operation.

morphic sequences, and more generally automatic sequences, are closed under non-erasing finite transductions and that non-erasure is the only obstruction to the transduction of sequences with dominant eigenvalues.
morphic sequences, and their transducts, are the only non-periodic alpha-substitutive sequences.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the eigenvalues of the substitution matrix are the key invariants for transduction of automatic sequences.
the transducts of morphic sequences are morphic and that the transduct of an alpha-substitutitive sequence is either alpha-substitutive or ultimately periodic.
the transductions which preserve alpha-substitutivty are precisely those which are induced by a single substitution with eigenvalue alpha.
The main takeaway from our work is that
non-erasure is the crucial condition for transduction of alpha-substitutive sequences.
the notion of substitutivity can be extended to non-erasing morphic sequences, and that this extension is useful to study the transduction of such sequences.
the eigenvalue of a morphic substitution can be used to characterize its transducts.
